extracted.intended_audience: general public; researchers, policy analysts, and practitioners seeking an overview of IFAD's structure, membership, and financing eligibility
extracted.subtask_description: Summarize IFAD's institutional rules and criteria: who may be a member, how members are categorized, governance organs (Governing Council, Executive Board, President), appointment/term rules, and interpretation of the Fund's mandate for financing. Useful for understanding eligibility and decision-making for IFAD funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership eligibility (Agreement Establishing IFAD, Art. 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: "Membership of the Fund shall be open to any State member of the United Nations, or of any of its specialized agencies, or of the International Atomic Energy Agency. Membership shall also be open to any groupings of States whose members have delegated to it powers in fields falling within the competence of the fund, and which is able to fulfil all the obligations of a Member of the Fund" (Art. 3, sec. 1 of the Agreement Establishing IFAD).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets the formal eligibility for joining IFAD; the article notes IFAD currently has 180 member states. Membership status determines rights/obligations and potential access to IFAD governance and resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership categorization: List A (high-income contributing members)
rubrics_metrics.description: List A includes high-income countries that contribute significantly to IFAD's financial resources. These nations have declared themselves ineligible for IFAD financing and do not qualify for Official Development Assistance (ODA) as defined by the OECD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List A members are primarily funders rather than recipients; the page lists 29 countries currently in List A and describes their role as providing funding for agricultural development initiatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership categorization: List B (OPEC / oil-rich contributors)
rubrics_metrics.description: List B includes member states from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) that also contribute to IFAD's resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List B comprises oil-rich countries that may be eligible for particular agricultural development initiatives; they contribute financially and may participate in deliberations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Membership categorization: List C (developing country recipients)
rubrics_metrics.description: List C includes developing nations eligible for IFAD money and services; this list is divided into three regional sub-lists: C1 (Africa), C2 (Europe, Asia, and the Pacific) and C3 (Latin America and Caribbean).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List C members are potential recipients of financing and services. The page enumerates the countries in each sub-list and indicates the regional breakdown used for representation and eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing Council: composition, powers, and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: "The Governing Council... holds full powers to make decisions. This council is composed of representatives from all IFAD Member States and gathers on an annual basis... The Governing Council has full authority over the fund's operations and makes decisions on important matters such as the approval of new members, the election of the President, issues concerning the permanent seat, the administrative budget, and the establishment of policies, criteria, and regulations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sessions are led by the Chairperson of the Bureau (one Chairperson and two Vice-chairpersons elected from Governors for two-year periods). The President participates in Governing Council meetings without voting rights. The Council is the principal decision-making organ, setting policies and the administrative framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Board: composition, election, and authority
rubrics_metrics.description: "The general operations of the fund are managed by the Executive Board, which exercises authority either directly provided by Agreement of Establishing the IFAD or delegated by the Governing Council. The Board is made up of 18 members and as many as 18 alternate members, all elected from the fund's members at the annual session of the Governing Council. Each member serves a three-year term within allocated Lists and Sub-Lists."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Board handles day-to-day oversight and operational decisions. The page includes a current framework listing member/alternate distribution by List and Sub-List, reflecting representational allocation across membership categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: President: appointment, term length, and extension rules
rubrics_metrics.description: "The president of the IFAD is appointed by the Governing Council with a two-thirds majority vote and serves a term of four years, renewable once. Under exceptional circumstances, the term may be extended by up to six months on the recommendation of the executive board."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appointment requires a supermajority of the Governing Council. Term limits and a narrow path for short extension are prescribed; these rules govern leadership continuity and renewal.

rubrics_metrics.name: President: roles, authorities, and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: "The president oversees the fund's operations, including organizing the staff and managing appointments and dismissals, following regulations set by the executive board. The president may appoint a vice-president to assist with assigned responsibilities and serves as the fund's legal representative... The president chairs the executive board, attending its meetings without voting privileges. The President also participates in Governing Council meetings without voting rights."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the President leads administration and represents the Fund legally, formal voting rights in the principal governing bodies are constrained (no vote in Executive Board or Governing Council meetings).

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Board chairing and President's voting status
rubrics_metrics.description: "The president chairs the executive board, attending its meetings without voting privileges."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This highlights the institutional separation between executive leadership and voting authority on the Board: the President leads meetings but does not hold a vote, leaving formal decision authority to elected Board members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Governing Bureau leadership selection and term
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sessions of the Governing Council are led by the Chairperson of the Bureau, which is made up of one Chairperson and two Vice-chairpersons, all elected from among the Governors of member states for a two-year period."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Bureau provides procedural leadership for Governing Council sessions; members are elected from governors and serve fixed two-year terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate interpretation and use of auxiliary/legal instruments
rubrics_metrics.description: IFAD has on occasion relied on interpretations and auxiliary instruments to extend its activities (for example, bypassing the original prerogative that 'the Fund can only finance its developing Member States and intergovernmental organizations in which those States participate' to extend financing to NGOs under certain conditions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page documents that IFAD's actions imply interpretations of its constituent instrument; such interpretive uses can extend the Fund's reach (e.g., financing NGOs or territories not formal members) but may provoke judicial or political challenges and risk membership contributions if activities are viewed as unauthorized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for financing (practical rule & exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Fund's original prerogative, financing is for developing Member States and intergovernmental organizations in which those States participate; however, in practice IFAD has extended financing beyond that prerogative under certain conditions (e.g., to NGOs, to territories such as the West Bank and Gaza via special funds/accords).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes the practical eligibility regime: List C developing members are eligible recipients, but IFAD has used legal instruments to reach populations or organizations beyond strict membership, subject to political and legal constraints.
